The animals view's 'Date created' and 'Date submitted' checks (notification-view-states.spec.ts:40, 183, 266) and the plants ones (review.spec.ts:412, 629) accept yesterday or today. The run's lease is state UP, and Docker came back with no containers (the stack sets no restart policies). items.before: An overnight branch run holds the lease as ibl-…, and a Homebrew cask upgrade quits Docker Desktop. The ladder's `tim build gate --phase e2e --holder ibl-…` starts Docker, rebuilds the stack, runs the e2e rungs green, then stops the stack and deletes the lease. The next stage runs `tim docker lease status`: lease null, up false. By RUN_STACK_RULE that means stackHeld with holder null, and confirmStackHeld believes it (null !== RUN_HOLDER). The run stops as 'stack-held' and preserves the attempt; or, where no stage checks, every later e2e gate cold-starts the stack and tears it down. Between gates the stack has no lease, so another session can take it. The end-of-run release finds nothing to release. The stackDown → recoverDownStack path only fires when a stage reads the lease before any gate has 'healed' it.

items.before: connectBoundedDispatcher() returns undefined whenever HTTP_PROXY is set, so fetchOnce (line 58) splits behaviour by environment. Unit, FIT and the local E2E stack (no HTTP_PROXY: docker/stack sets none) send through npm undici 8.11.2's fetch, with an undici FormData copy and a private Agent. CDP, which injects HTTP_PROXY, sends through Node's built-in fetch, with Node's FormData, through the global ProxyAgent. The comment at lines 17-20 says the fork is needed because built-in fetch 'rejects' npm undici agents. The pre-fix logs show otherwise. inc-109-ladder-e2e-rerun at 20:13Z, before 19a76c54 at 20:26Z, shows built-in fetch already connecting through /home/node/node_modules/undici/lib/core/connect.js with a 10000ms timeout. This is because npm undici's lib/global.js installs its Agent under both 'undici.globalDispatcher.2' and, wrapped in a Dispatcher1Wrapper, the legacy '.1' symbol. So the parallel fetch was never needed. In CDP the change adds nothing: there is no 2s bound, and the retry fires only if the socket to the squid proxy itself fails. A backend the proxy cannot reach comes back as a 502/503 response (http target) or as RequestAbortedError 'Proxy response (503) !== 200 when HTTP Tunneling' (https target), and neither is in CONNECT_ERROR_CODES.

- CDP, which injects HTTP_PROXY, sends through Node's built-in fetch, with Node's FormData, through the global ProxyAgent.

This is because npm undici's lib/global.js installs its Agent under both:

items.before: Confirmed. countries/index.js:17 (untouched by the diff, but it is the main 5xx path the new errors.js logging is for) calls Boom.serverUnavailable(message, data). @hapi/boom 'serverUnavailable(message, data)' passes data through internals.serverError to options.data (lib/index.js:117-118, 381-383), and boom never sets err.cause, so response.cause is undefined. The dashboard controller rethrows Boom errors (controller.js:114-115), so an unreachable reference-data service reaches catchAll as a 503 and stackWithCauses prints only the Boom stack, with no 'Caused by:'. One correction: the test shape (Boom.boomify of a TypeError with a cause) is not impossible. It is exactly what hapi does to an uncaught non-Boom error thrown from a handler, so the new code does work for uncaught throws. It does not work for the countries outage, which is the one fetch path this app wraps in Boom itself. Fix as suggested: boomify the original error with statusCode 503, or keep the cause on the Boom.
items.after:
Confirmed.

countries/index.js:17 calls Boom.serverUnavailable(message, data). The diff does not touch it, but it is the main 5xx path the new errors.js logging is for.

- @hapi/boom 'serverUnavailable(message, data)' passes data through internals.serverError to options.data (lib/index.js:117-118, 381-383).
- boom never sets err.cause, so response.cause is undefined.
- The dashboard controller rethrows Boom errors (controller.js:114-115).
- So an unreachable reference-data service reaches catchAll as a 503. stackWithCauses prints only the Boom stack, with no 'Caused by:'.

One correction: the test shape (Boom.boomify of a TypeError with a cause) is not impossible.

It is exactly what hapi does to an uncaught non-Boom error thrown from a handler. So the new code does work for uncaught throws.

It does not work for the countries outage, which is the one fetch path this app wraps in Boom itself.

Fix as suggested: boomify the original error with statusCode 503, or keep the cause on the Boom.
